data.name: Uruguay
data.summary: Uruguay taxes residents' foreign interest and dividends at 12% and, since 1 January 2026, also foreign capital gains (12% of the gain, or an elective 2.4% of sale price). New residents from 2026 can opt for an 11-year holiday on foreign capital income if they spend 183 days a year or make a qualifying investment (USD 2m real estate or about USD 100k a year in funds). There is no inheritance tax (3% ITP on inherited Uruguayan real estate) and a 0.1% wealth tax on Uruguayan assets only.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence
regimes.description: Residents pay IRPF at a flat 12% on capital income, including foreign interest and dividends and, from 1 Jan 2026 (Law 20.446), foreign capital gains and foreign rents. Dividends from Uruguayan companies 7%. Net wealth tax at 0.1% on Uruguay-located net assets above about UYU 6.65m.
regimes.eligibility: Resident if 183+ days, or centre of vital/economic interests in Uruguay (spouse and minor children living in Uruguay create a presumption), or qualifying Uruguayan investments.

capital_gains.summary: From 1 Jan 2026, gains on foreign movable assets (e.g. foreign shares) and foreign real estate are taxable at 12% of the actual gain; the taxpayer may instead elect a deemed gain of 20% of the sale price (2.4% of price) or 15% for real estate (1.8%). Gains on Uruguayan shares 12%; titles issued by Uruguayan entities effectively 2.4%.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Real estate transfer tax (ITP) 2% each for buyer and seller on Uruguayan property.

regimes.name: Tax holiday for new residents (Law 20.446, from 2026)
regimes.description: Individuals becoming tax resident from 1 Jan 2026 may elect to be taxed under IRNR (non-resident tax, territorial) on foreign capital income and gains for the year of arrival plus 10 years. Foreign dividends, interest and gains are then untaxed. The former permanent 7% option is not available to 2026 arrivals.
regimes.eligibility: New tax residence from 2026. If residence is via 183 days' presence: no investment needed, presence must be kept each year. If via centre of interests or investments: real estate over UI 12,500,000 (about USD 2m) or annual fund capitalisation of UI 625,000 (about USD 100,000) in productive/research projects.

capital_gains.summary: Foreign gains not taxed during the holiday; Uruguayan-source gains taxed as usual.

income.name: Uruguay

income_tax.summary: Uruguay taxes employment income of residents with IRPF at 0% to 36% (annual scale in UYU, as at 31 December 2025), and social security of about 18-23% of salary for employees. New tax residents can claim a tax holiday: no IRPF on foreign-source income for the year of application plus ten years. Montevideo adds no local income tax.
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Self-employed (empresa unipersonal / monotributo) contribute through BPS. The 22.6% rate is the sum of the PwC 2026 components for the owner acting as both employee and employer: 15% employee retirement + 7.5% employer retirement + 0.1% labour restructuring fund (it also equals the BPS 2026 table excerpt of UYU 2,088 on a UYU 9,240 base noted in an earlier pass). Retirement rates apply only up to UYU 288,826 a month until 31 Dec 2026 (PwC), so the cap is 12 x that; health cover (FONASA, 8% of one BPC if not opting into the national health system per the earlier excerpt) is not added. The BPS page itself could not be reached, so the owner's exact base and health contribution are unverified.
income_tax.local_tax_note: No local income tax. The scale is for resident employees (PwC lists it as at 31 Dec 2025; thresholds are indexed yearly). Pension contributions are capped at UYU 288,826 a month until 31 Dec 2026; employee rate 0.196 = 15% pension + 4.5% health (single, no dependants, above 2.5 BPC) + 0.1% FRL, health continues above the cap.

Uruguay: social_security_deductible left null. DGI's IRPF guide (category II) lists BPS retirement, FONASA and FRL contributions among the 'deducciones', but they do not reduce the taxed base: IRPF on the deductions (14% if nominal income is up to 180 BPC, otherwise 8%) is subtracted from the tax computed on income. The field cannot express a credit; as a deduction-equivalent it is about 0.25 at the marginal rate of a USD 60k earner, which has not been verified.

regimes.name: Hoja/Cedula de Identidad Provisoria - digital nomad
regimes.description: Special residence permit for people who work remotely, self-employed or for foreign companies. Apply online after entering as a tourist; first permit of 180 days, extendable once by 180 days (maximum about one year). Applicants make a sworn statement of means; no minimum amount is published. Renewal needs criminal-record certificates and a Uruguayan vaccination certificate.
regimes.duration_note: Six months plus one six-month extension.

regimes.name: New-resident tax holiday (foreign income exempt from IRPF)
regimes.description: New tax residents are exempt from IRPF on income earned abroad for the year of application and the ten following years (11 years). From 2026, new applicants qualify through more than 183 days of physical presence in the calendar year, or by investment (real estate above about USD 2.1 million or about USD 105,000 a year into 'Uruguay Innova'). It does not cover Uruguayan-source income, which stays taxed at the IRPF scale. Uruguay's source principle makes income from activities developed in Uruguay (PwC) Uruguayan-source, so a remote worker's pay for work done while living in Uruguay is not covered; the holiday covers income earned abroad, in practice foreign-source capital income.
regimes.duration_note: Year of application plus ten years; those who opted before end-2025 keep their original terms.

succession.name: Uruguay
succession.summary: Children, parents and a spouse are protected: with one child half the estate is reserved, with two two thirds, with three or more three quarters (Civil Code art. 887). Without descendants, ascendants have half. Uruguay has a trust law (fideicomiso) but trusts cannot be used to override the reserved share, and I found no private-foundation regime.
succession.reserved_share: Legítima for descendants: 1/2 with one child, 2/3 with two, 3/4 with three or more (Código Civil art. 887, as amended by Ley 15.855). Without descendants, 1/2 for ascendants. A spouse counts as a child when descendants exist; otherwise the spousal portion is 1/4 (art. 881).
succession.foreign_law_note: Not sourced. Uruguay has a general private international law statute (Ley 19.920 of 2020) and the Montevideo Treaties, but the succession conflict rule and any choice of law were not read.
succession.trust_note: Fideicomiso is governed by Ley 17.703 (2003). It cannot defeat the legítima. Uruguay is not a party to the Hague Trusts Convention. Foundations: civil-law fundaciones for public-benefit purposes exist; a private-interest foundation was not found and the rule was not sourced.
open_questions: The conflict rule for succession and any choice of law (Ley 19.920) was not read.
The spouse's reserved share was taken from a summary of Ley 15.855 and Ley 16.603; confirm art. 881 on impo.com.uy.
Law governing foundations (fundaciones) and whether a family foundation is possible was not sourced.
Treatment of foreign trusts was not sourced.

immigration.name: Uruguay
immigration.summary: Uruguay gives legal residence without any investment: proof of lawful income, housing and a clean record is enough, and Mercosur-area nationals have an easier route. A separate tax regime from 1 January 2026 grants an 11-year foreign-income tax holiday for buying about USD 2.1 million of property or investing about USD 105,000 a year in innovation funds. Remote workers get a 6-month renewable visa with no income test.
immigration.naturalisation: Five years of legal residence for single applicants, three years for married applicants living with their family; Spanish, clean record.
immigration.dual_citizenship_note: Uruguay does not require renunciation of another nationality (general position; not source-checked in this session).

routes.name: Legal residence (temporary or permanent)
routes.summary: Ordinary residence in Uruguay needs no investment: apply with proof of lawful income, housing, clean record and health certificate. Right to work comes with the residence card.
routes.requirements: Applications to the Direccion Nacional de Migracion. Chambers states there are no quotas or investment requirements for immigration; proof of income at least the national minimum wage (the page is inconsistent on the exact figure); criminal record, health card. Uruguay has no standalone work permit: the right to work comes from the residence card. Fees for residence not stated in the source.
routes.physical_presence: Not stated in the sources reviewed; residence is kept by living in Uruguay
routes.family: Spouses and children may apply; married applicants living with family qualify for citizenship earlier.
routes.tax_note: Legal residence does not by itself decide tax residence (183 days, centre of interests or the investment presumptions apply).

routes.name: Tax residence by investment (new regime from 1 January 2026)
routes.summary: A 11-year tax holiday on foreign income for new tax residents who buy about USD 2.1 million of Uruguayan property or put about USD 105,000 a year into 'Uruguay Innova' funds. Presence of 183 days is the alternative.
routes.requirements: From 1 January 2026 (Law 20.446, Decree 188/026 per Andersen): for people without tax residence elsewhere, either urban real estate over UI 12,500,000 (about USD 2.1 million; the computable value rises 50% for interior property) or UI 625,000 a year (about USD 105,000) in 'Uruguay Innova' funds, or more than 183 days a year. Tax holiday for the year of application plus 10 years (11 total), then ordinary IRPF, or a 50% IRPF cut for 5 more years with a further USD 1.05 million of property, or a fixed annual fee of USD 200,000 to 315,000 for up to 20 years. People who opted into the previous regime (about UI 3.5 million property plus 60 days, or UI 15 million in a company with 15 jobs) before the end of 2025 keep their conditions. This is a tax-residence regime; immigration residence is a separate application.
routes.investment_options: UI 12,500,000 (about USD 2.062 million) in property; or UI 625,000 a year in Uruguay Innova funds; or 183+ days a year with no investment.
routes.fees_note: The minimum is stated in unidades indexadas (UI); USD figures are the sources' approximations.
routes.physical_presence: More than 183 days a year, or the investment test (check Decree 188/026 for any minimum days)
routes.tax_note: New tax residents: exemption of foreign-source income for the year of application plus 10 years (IRNR exemption period).

routes.summary: Six-month visa for unsponsored remote workers, renewable once for six months. No minimum income; a good-faith affidavit is used.
